source.quote: Under `claude -p` the project's `permissions.allow` rules are ignored until the workspace is trusted (`~/.claude.json projects[<main clone>].hasTrustDialogAccepted`); the first real worker ended with a HANDOFF.md listing every denied command.

prompt: Write check-trust.sh in the current directory, run as `bash check-trust.sh <claude-json-file> <project-dir>`. The JSON file has the shape {"projects": {"<project-dir>": {"hasTrustDialogAccepted": true}}}. Exit 0 only when that project's hasTrustDialogAccepted is true. Otherwise (false, missing key, missing project, missing file) exit 1 and print a line containing launch-trust. Reply with the single word done.

checks.name: untrusted project is refused with launch-trust
checks.command: d=$(mktemp -d) && printf '{"projects":{"/p":{}}}' > $d/b.json && ! bash check-trust.sh $d/b.json /p >/dev/null 2>&1 && bash check-trust.sh $d/b.json /p 2>&1 | grep -q launch-trust
